name.en: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries

nature.en: Intergovernmental organization of oil-exporting countries (commodity producers' cartel)
nature.zh: 石油出口國的政府間組織（原物料生產國卡特爾）

purpose.en: Oil-exporting countries coordinate their oil policies and production levels to influence world oil prices and secure stable revenues.
purpose.zh: 石油出口國協調石油政策與產量，以影響國際油價並確保穩定收入。

notes: UAE (member since 1967) announced on 28 Apr 2026 (WAM) its exit from OPEC and OPEC+, effective 1 May 2026; it is therefore excluded. Caveat: a secondary source reports OPEC's website still listed the UAE as of early Nov 2026 and OPEC issued no statement; the UAE no longer appears in the OPEC+ voluntary-adjustment group after May 2026. OPEC now has 11 members.
Former members: Qatar (left 2019), Ecuador (left 2020), Angola (left 1 Jan 2024), Indonesia (suspended 2016), UAE (left 2026).

Judgement call: the 10 non-OPEC Declaration of Cooperation (OPEC+) countries are shown as 'partner' because OPEC+ jointly sets output and is central to teaching oil-market policy. Brazil is also shown as 'partner' but only under the looser Charter of Cooperation (no quotas) - see its note.
